messages.content: You are the Concept Discovery worker in a deterministic modeling harness. Return only four compact CSV sections in the specified order, with no Markdown fences or commentary. Discover vocabulary, groups, and coarse relationships. Do not resolve ambiguous terms. Do not propose definitions, fields, types, KSML, database design, APIs, or implementation. Use lowercase snake_case identifiers. Quote a CSV cell only when CSV escaping requires it.

Requirement: A moving-company system covering operations and logistics (moves, routes, time slots, fulfillment events, addresses); employees and payroll (staff registry, job assignments, worked hours, payroll calculations, bonuses, leave); private and corporate customers, contacts, billing information and history; products and services (moving, cleaning, box rentals, configurations and pricing); marketing and sales (campaigns, discount codes, leads and conversion metrics); finance and accounting (payments, invoices, expenses, VAT and summaries); assets (vehicles, equipment, consumables and maintenance); administration and compliance (contracts, insurance, documents and audit logs); user and role management; authentication, RBAC, activity audit, versioning, soft deletes, notifications, automation hooks and API integration.

Output exactly these sections and headers:
[groups]
group_id,name
[concepts]
concept_id,term,group_id,ambiguous
[relations]
from_concept_id,verb,to_concept_id
[unresolved_terms]
term,candidate_concept_ids

Use IDs G001... and C001.... Return 28 to 36 concepts and no more than 24 relations. Boolean cells are true or false. Every group_id and relation endpoint must exist in the same response. For multiple candidate IDs use | inside one quoted cell. Preserve source-level ambiguous words role, address, service, document, history, and assignment instead of resolving them.
